# Drawing

## `Canvas`

```python
Canvas(page: Page, *, underlay: bool = False)
```

Drawing on one page in paint order, written as one content stream.

Get one with `Page.draw` and use it in a `with` block: the
drawing is written when the block ends normally, in one transaction and
one undo step, and discarded after an exception. Everything is in
display coordinates, the top-left-origin space of `Page.rect`,
and drawn in the order of the calls, over the page's content or, with
`underlay=True`, beneath it.

Paths take a `fill` `Color` and a `stroke`, a `Stroke`
or a `Color` for a 1-point line; a path with neither is stroked
with a 1-point black line. A color's alpha below 1 paints it
translucent. A `LinearGradient` or a `RadialGradient` paints
wherever a color does on a path, a shape, or text, and stops that differ in alpha
paint through a soft mask, so that a fill and a stroke are then two
paintings. Equal gradient objects are written once in a canvas. A gradient
renders within 8 levels of 255 per channel of what its stops say at 72 dpi
in hayro and poppler, and one that repeats within 16, away from its sharp
changes and from the edges of what it paints. The scopes `clip`, `transform`,
`opacity`, `blend`, `layer`, and `tag` are
context managers that apply to everything drawn inside them. `text` and `textbox` draw
text in a Standard 14 or embedded OpenType `Font`.

A canvas holds at most 1,048,576 path points, of paths and clips
together, nests at most 16 scopes, and writes at most 64 MiB of
content; a gradient has at most 1,048,576 stops, and repeats at most
4,096 times over what it paints; more raise `LimitError` with code
`content_element_count` or `content_input_size`, or
`ValueError` for the nesting. A gradient whose line has no extent, whose
ends are one point or whose circles are one circle, raises `ValueError`
when it is drawn.

### `text`

```python
Canvas.text(
    text: str | Sequence[TextSpan],
    at: Sequence[float],
    *,
    font: Font | None = None,
    fallback_fonts: Sequence[Font] | FallbackFonts = (),
    size: float = 11,
    fill: Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0, colorspace=None, components=None),
    stroke: Stroke | Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    render_mode: TextRenderMode | str | None = None,
    direction: Literal['horizontal', 'vertical'] = 'horizontal',
    base_direction: TextDirection = 'auto',
    line_height: float | None = None,
    rotate: int = 0,
    max_text_size: int | None = 1048576,
)
```

Draw text or styled `TextSpan` runs whose first baseline starts at `at`.

Pass a `str` or a sequence of `TextSpan` runs to mix fonts,
sizes, colours, render modes, underlines, strikethroughs, and inline
`/Link` annotations on the same line. Lines break on explicit line
separators and are spaced `line_height` times `size` apart (by
default at the font's own line height, or the tallest run's ascent and
descent when font sizes mix). `base_direction` sets the UAX #9
bidirectional paragraph base direction (`"auto"`, `"ltr"`, or
`"rtl"`); `base_direction="rtl"` cannot be combined with
`direction="vertical"`. `rotate` turns the text clockwise about
`at` by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees, so that at 90 the lines run down
the page and stack leftward; `transform` turns it by any other
angle. `font` defaults to Helvetica. Pass `fallback_fonts`—an
ordered sequence of `Font` faces or a document's
`Document.fallback_fonts`—to resolve missing grapheme clusters
deterministically across faces without any global font registry; only
faces that draw at least one glyph are embedded. Text is filled,
stroked, both, or—with `render_mode=TextRenderMode.INVISIBLE`—emitted
invisibly (`3 Tr`) so it leaves no ink while remaining searchable and
extractable. To clip subsequent drawings to glyph outlines
(`4 Tr`–`7 Tr`), use `clip_text`. Pass
`direction="vertical"` with embedded OpenType faces to shape and
embed vertical text (`Identity-V` and `/W2`), where glyphs run
downward from `at` and subsequent columns stack right-to-left. Any
`/Link` annotations from `TextSpan.link` commit inside the same
canvas transaction and undo step, and are discarded if the canvas
aborts. Fill and stroke accept a `LinearGradient` or
`RadialGradient`, in the canvas coordinate space. If a soft mask
requires separate fill and stroke objects, the second uses empty
`ActualText` so extraction reads the text once. Gradient tolerances
are those of `Canvas`. The text is limited to 1 MiB of UTF-8,
65,536 spans, and 4,096 lines by default (`max_text_size`, `None`
for trusted input), refused with `LimitError` code
`text_input_size`, `content_element_count`, or `text_line_count`.
A colour glyph that COLR paints or a PNG strike holds draws in its own
colours, which `fill` and `stroke` do not change, except for a COLR
layer in the text's colour, which takes the fill. Any other colour
glyph with no outline in an OpenType face raises `PdfError`,
naming the character, the glyph, and the paint; see `Font`.

### `textbox`

```python
Canvas.textbox(
    rect: Sequence[float],
    text: str | Sequence[TextSpan],
    *,
    font: Font | None = None,
    fallback_fonts: Sequence[Font] | FallbackFonts = (),
    size: float = 11,
    align: TextAlign = 'left',
    line_height: float | None = None,
    fill: Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0, colorspace=None, components=None),
    stroke: Stroke | Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    render_mode: TextRenderMode | str | None = None,
    direction: Literal['horizontal', 'vertical'] = 'horizontal',
    base_direction: TextDirection = 'auto',
    rotate: int = 0,
    max_text_size: int | None = 1048576,
) -> TextFit
```

Wrap text or styled `TextSpan` runs inside `rect` and report how they fit.

Lines break in logical order at Unicode line-break opportunities
(UAX #14) and, for a word wider than the box, between grapheme
clusters (UAX #29), followed by per-line UAX #9 bidirectional visual
reordering. `align` supports physical `"left"`, `"center"`,
`"right"`, and `"justify"`, as well as direction-aware `"start"`
and `"end"` (left/right for LTR paragraphs, right/left for RTL).
`base_direction` controls UAX #9 paragraph base direction
(`"auto"`, `"ltr"`, or `"rtl"`); `base_direction="rtl"` cannot
be combined with `direction="vertical"`. Lines are placed as
`text` places them: in horizontal mode, the first baseline sits
one ascent below the top of `rect` and the text fits when the last
line's descender fits inside `rect`; in vertical mode
(`direction="vertical"`), columns run downward along the box height
and stack right-to-left from its right edge. When the text does not
fit, nothing is drawn (including decorations and `TextSpan.link`
annotations) and `TextFit.spare_height` is the negative
shortfall; `Font.text_height` measures the height that plain text
needs without drawing it. Tabs become single spaces. `rotate` turns
the text clockwise inside `rect` by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees: at 90
horizontal lines run down the box and stack from its right edge
leftward, so they wrap at the box's height and fill its width, and at
270 they run up and stack from the left edge. The `font`,
`fallback_fonts`, `fill`, `stroke`, `render_mode`,
`direction`, and `size` options follow `text`, and text that
fits refuses as there: a colour glyph with no outline raises
`PdfError`.

### `clip_text`

```python
Canvas.clip_text(
    text: str,
    at: Sequence[float],
    *,
    font: Font | None = None,
    fallback_fonts: Sequence[Font] | FallbackFonts = (),
    size: float = 11,
    fill: Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    stroke: Stroke | Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    direction: Literal['horizontal', 'vertical'] = 'horizontal',
    line_height: float | None = None,
    rotate: int = 0,
    max_text_size: int | None = 1048576,
) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Clip what the block draws to the glyph outlines of `text` (`4 Tr`–`7 Tr`).

With neither `fill` nor `stroke` (the default), the text clips
without painting ink (`7 Tr`). Passing `fill`, `stroke`, or both
also paints the text while adding its outlines to the clipping path
(`4 Tr`, `5 Tr`, or `6 Tr`). Bitmap-only fonts without glyph
outlines cannot clip and raise `PdfError`.

### `image`

```python
Canvas.image(
    rect: Sequence[float],
    source: str | os.PathLike[str] | bytes | bytearray | memoryview | Pixmap | PageImage | int,
    *,
    keep_aspect: bool = True,
    rotate: int = 0,
)
```

Draw a JPEG, PNG, or JPEG 2000 image, a `Pixmap`, or an image of this document into `rect`.

An encoded image is a path or bytes; JPEG and JPEG 2000 data is
stored as it is, and PNG data is decoded and stored with Flate, its
alpha as a soft mask. A `Pixmap` is stored as PNG data would
be. An image of this document, a `PageImage` or the object
number of an image XObject, is drawn again without a copy.
`rotate` turns the image clockwise by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees,
and `keep_aspect` centres it in `rect` at its aspect ratio. The
same encoded image drawn several times, by any canvas of the
document, is stored once.

### `page`

```python
Canvas.page(
    rect: Sequence[float],
    source: Page | Content,
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    keep_aspect: bool = True,
    rotate: int = 0,
)
```

Draw another page, of any open document or this one, into `rect`.

The page is placed as a Form XObject, as vector content with its
fonts and images: its content, geometry and resources are read
from one version of its document, and its resources are copied
with the objects they reach as they are when this call is made, so
a later edit of the source does not change the placed page. `clip` is a rectangle
in the source page's display coordinates, those of its
`Page.rect`: only the part of the page inside it is drawn,
scaled into `rect` in place of the whole page. `rotate` turns
the page, or its clipped part, clockwise by 0, 90, 180, or 270
degrees, and `keep_aspect` centres it in `rect` at its aspect
ratio after the turn. A page placed several times, by any canvas of
this document, is stored once while its content, its geometry and
every object its resources reach are unchanged.
A live page omits annotations and form fields. A complete `Content`
uses the geometry, resources and annotation setting captured by
`Page.content`. Visible captured appearances become vector content.

### `draw`

```python
Canvas.draw(item: Path | Image | TextRun)
```

Paint a `Path`, `Image`, or `TextRun` from `Page.content`.

The item's clips, its groups' opacity and blend modes, and its own
blend mode are applied; soft masks are not. An axial or radial
`ShadingPattern` retains the color function read from its
document version. Its RGB approximation is sampled on the first
drawing, preserving its matrix, domain, opacity, and extension at
either end, its clip box, and its background. Sampling is bounded
to 1,025 stops; features between the probes can be lost. A
`TilingPattern` retains its captured pattern cell and is
written as a bounded `/PatternType 1` stream preserving its cell
box, steps, matrix, and opacity; cells containing soft masks,
function/mesh shadings, or excessive nesting raise `ValueError`.
Function-based and mesh shadings cannot be drawn yet.

An indirect image or stencil image mask is drawn from its object, with
the image's own masks: a canvas on a page of the item's document draws
that object again, and one of another document copies it, with the
objects it reaches but pages, as it is when this call is made. Inline
raster images and inline stencil image masks (`xref == 0`) promote
their captured payloads into bounded, deduplicated image XObjects.
Stencil masks paint with their `Image.fill` paint.

A text run uses its original PDF codes and positioned text matrices.
Its font dictionary, encoding, and embedded program are copied from
the version that was read, including when drawing on the same document.
Simple embedded and standard 14 fonts, embedded Identity-H/V fonts, and
Type 3 fonts with their own resources are supported. Runs with a fallback
or direct font, Type 3 procedures that need enclosing resources,
other composite encodings, a singular glyph transform, replacement
text, a soft mask, or a pattern paint raise `ValueError`. A closed source raises
`DocumentClosedError`. These refusals draw nothing.

### `transform`

```python
Canvas.transform(matrix: Matrix | Sequence[float]) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Transform what the block draws by `matrix`, applied before the enclosing transforms.

### `opacity`

```python
Canvas.opacity(
    alpha: float,
    *,
    isolated: bool = False,
    knockout: bool = False,
    colorspace: Literal['gray', 'rgb', 'cmyk'] | None = None,
) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Composite the block as a transparency group and draw it at `alpha`.

An isolated group starts with a transparent backdrop. In a knockout group
each element replaces earlier elements in its shape. An isolated group
may declare its device blending colour space. Other groups inherit it.

### `soft_mask`

```python
Canvas.soft_mask(
    group: Stream,
    *,
    subtype: SoftMaskType | str = SoftMaskType.ALPHA,
) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Mask the block with an existing transparency Form XObject from this document.

Alpha uses the group's computed opacity. Luminosity uses its colour and
requires an explicit group blending space. The mask applies inside the
block and the enclosing graphics state resumes afterwards.

### `blend`

```python
Canvas.blend(mode: BlendMode | str) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Blend what the block draws with the content below it.

### `layer`

```python
Canvas.layer(layer: Layer | LayerMembership) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Draw the block as optional content of a `Layer` or a `LayerMembership`.

What the block draws shows only while `layer`, a group of the
page's document or a membership of its groups, is visible, in
rendering, text extraction, and viewers. The block is written as
`/OC` marked content; a membership is written as a new membership
dictionary. A group that is no longer an optional
content group when the canvas commits raises
`StaleObjectError`. Use a `Layer` returned by this
document's `Document.layers`: a manually constructed or
unpickled value has no document of origin and cannot be drawn.

### `tag`

```python
Canvas.tag(
    role: TagRole | str,
    *,
    alt: str | None = None,
    lang: str | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    actual_text: str | None = None,
    expanded: str | None = None,
    scope: TableHeaderScope | str | None = None,
    numbering: ListNumbering | str | None = None,
) -> AbstractContextManager[None]
```

Make what the block draws a structure element of the document's structure tree.

Scopes nest into the structure tree in the order of the calls.
`TagRole.ARTIFACT` marks content outside the logical
structure, as is everything drawn outside any tag scope of a
document that already has a structure tree. `alt` is the
alternate description that figures and formulas need, `title` the
element's title, `lang` its BCP 47 language, `actual_text` the
text that replaces its content for extraction and assistive
technology, and `expanded` the expanded form of an abbreviation
(`/E`, ISO 32000-2 section 14.9.5). `scope` says what a
`TagRole.TABLE_HEADER` cell heads, and `numbering` how a
`TagRole.LIST` numbers its items; other roles take neither.

The elements join the document's structure tree, created when it
has none, under its `Document` element when the root holds that
one element only. The canvas's drawing is then written as a Form
XObject with a `/StructParents` key of its own, in which each
element names its marked content. A tag scope cannot start inside an
`opacity` scope or an artifact.

## `ListNumbering`

How a list numbers its items (ISO 32000-1 section 14.8.5.5), by its PDF name.

Members: `NONE`, `DISC`, `CIRCLE`, `SQUARE`, `DECIMAL`, `LOWER_ROMAN`, `UPPER_ROMAN`, `LOWER_ALPHA`, `UPPER_ALPHA`.

## `PathBuilder`

```python
PathBuilder()
```

Geometry for `Canvas.path` and `Canvas.clip`, built from segments.

Every method adds segments in display coordinates and returns the
builder, so calls chain: `PathBuilder().move_to(a).line_to(b).close()`.
The constructors (`rect`, `ellipse`, `circle`,
`polygon`, `sector`, `zigzag`, and `wave`) each
add complete subpaths.

### `segments`

```python
PathBuilder.segments: tuple[Segment, ...]
```

The segments added so far.

### `current_point`

```python
PathBuilder.current_point: Point | None
```

The end of the last segment, or `None` before the first.

### `move_to`

```python
PathBuilder.move_to(point: Sequence[float]) -> Self
```

Start a subpath at `point`.

### `line_to`

```python
PathBuilder.line_to(point: Sequence[float]) -> Self
```

Add a line to `point`.

### `curve_to`

```python
PathBuilder.curve_to(
    control1: Sequence[float],
    control2: Sequence[float],
    point: Sequence[float],
) -> Self
```

Add a cubic Bézier curve to `point`.

### `quad_to`

```python
PathBuilder.quad_to(control: Sequence[float], point: Sequence[float]) -> Self
```

Add a quadratic Bézier curve to `point`, as the equal cubic curve.

### `close`

```python
PathBuilder.close() -> Self
```

Close the current subpath with a line to its start.

### `rect`

```python
PathBuilder.rect(rect: Sequence[float], *, radius: float = 0) -> Self
```

Add a rectangle, with corners rounded by `radius` points.

### `ellipse`

```python
PathBuilder.ellipse(rect: Sequence[float]) -> Self
```

Add the ellipse inside `rect`.

### `circle`

```python
PathBuilder.circle(center: Sequence[float], radius: float) -> Self
```

Add a circle.

### `polygon`

```python
PathBuilder.polygon(points: Iterable[Sequence[float]], *, close: bool = True) -> Self
```

Add straight segments through `points`, closed unless `close` is false.

### `sector`

```python
PathBuilder.sector(
    center: Sequence[float],
    radius: float,
    start: float,
    sweep: float,
    *,
    pie: bool = True,
) -> Self
```

Add an arc of `sweep` degrees around `center`, from `start` degrees.

Angles run clockwise on the page from the positive x axis. With
`pie`, lines join the arc's ends to the centre, which closes it.

### `zigzag`

```python
PathBuilder.zigzag(

```

Add a zigzag line from `start` to `end` whose teeth are `breadth` points wide.

```python
PathBuilder.wave(

```

Add a wavy line from `start` to `end` whose waves are `breadth` points wide.

## `PathInput`

```python
PathInput: TypeAlias = PathBuilder | Path | Iterable[Segment]
```

## `TableHeaderScope`

What a table header cell heads (ISO 32000-1 section 14.8.5.7), by its PDF name.

Members: `ROW`, `COLUMN`, `BOTH`.

## `TagRole`

A structure type (ISO 32000-1 section 14.8.4), by its PDF name.

`ARTIFACT` marks content that is not part of the document's
logical structure, such as page headers, footers, and decoration.

Members: `PART`, `ARTICLE`, `SECTION`, `DIV`, `BLOCK_QUOTE`, `CAPTION`, `TOC`, `TOC_ITEM`, `INDEX`, `NON_STRUCT`, `PARAGRAPH`, `HEADING_1`, `HEADING_2`, `HEADING_3`, `HEADING_4`, `HEADING_5`, `HEADING_6`, `LIST`, `LIST_ITEM`, `LABEL`, `LIST_BODY`, `TABLE`, `TABLE_ROW`, `TABLE_HEADER`, `TABLE_DATA`, `TABLE_HEAD`, `TABLE_BODY`, `TABLE_FOOT`, `SPAN`, `QUOTE`, `NOTE`, `REFERENCE`, `BIB_ENTRY`, `CODE`, `FIGURE`, `FORMULA`, `ARTIFACT`, `LINK`.

## `TextAlign`

```python
TextAlign: TypeAlias = Literal['left', 'center', 'right', 'justify', 'start', 'end']
```

Horizontal alignment accepted by `Canvas.textbox`: physical
`"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, or direction-aware
`"start"` and `"end"` (resolved per paragraph against its UAX #9 base
direction).

## `TextDirection`

```python
TextDirection: TypeAlias = Literal['auto', 'ltr', 'rtl']
```

Paragraph base direction for UAX #9 bidirectional layout on
`Canvas.text` and `Canvas.textbox`: `"auto"` determines the base
direction per paragraph from its first strong directional character (UAX #9
P2/P3), while `"ltr"` and `"rtl"` force left-to-right or right-to-left.

## `TextFit`

```python
TextFit(*, spare_height: float)
```

How text fits a `Canvas.textbox`: the height left below its last line.

In horizontal mode, `spare_height` is the height remaining below the
last line; in vertical mode, it is the width remaining past the last
column. A negative `spare_height` is the shortfall of text that did
not fit, and was not drawn.

### `fits`

```python
TextFit.fits: bool
```

Whether the text fit its box and was drawn.

## `TextSpan`

```python
TextSpan(
    *,
    text: str,
    font: Font | None = None,
    size: float | None = None,
    fill: Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    stroke: Stroke | Color | Gradient | PatternPaint | None = None,
    render_mode: TextRenderMode | str | None = None,
    underline: bool = False,
    strikethrough: bool = False,
    link: Target | None = None,
)
```

One inline styled run inside `Canvas.text` or `Canvas.textbox`.

Fields set to `None` inherit the enclosing call's defaults (`font`,
`size`, `fill`, `stroke`, `render_mode`). To draw a single
stroke-only or invisible span inside a filled paragraph, set
`render_mode=TextRenderMode.STROKE` (with `stroke=...`) or
`render_mode=TextRenderMode.INVISIBLE`.
